reason: Controller raw-evidence review found one E-2 contract blocker. Design §10 E2-4 requires ToolContext auditSink to be a host-agnostic duck type mirroring AuditLogger.log(entry), and E2-6 requires Alembic ToolContextFactory to pass auditSink: tryGet('auditLogger'). Alembic/lib/tools/adapters/terminal-adapter/TerminalAudit.ts also recognizes only sink.log(...). AlembicAgent commit b2088045 instead defines ToolAuditSinkLike.record(event), terminal.ts calls sink.record(event), and runtime-terminal-safety tests only cover record(). This would force the next Alembic host-wiring step to add an adapter/wrapper instead of consuming the agreed contract, so the producer result is not acceptable yet. Rework must align the Agent contract/tests to .log(entry) and preserve hash-only/no-raw-command/non-fatal audit semantics without expanding scope.

Controller raw-evidence review found the rework fixed the method/shape drift (.log(entry) and data.commandHash), but introduced a remaining E-2 audit persistence blocker: AlembicAgent/src/tools/runtime/handlers/terminal.ts builds requestId as terminal.exec:<commandHash-prefix>. Alembic AuditLogger.log uses entry.requestId as audit_logs.id, and audit_logs.id is TEXT PRIMARY KEY. Therefore repeated executions of the same command produce the same audit id; the second insert fails and is swallowed by AuditLogger/terminal audit non-fatal handling, so the requirement that every live terminal.exec leaves an audit entry is still false. This is in-scope for E-2; rework must not expand scope, but must make requestId absent (letting AuditLogger generate a unique id) or otherwise unique per invocation, and add a regression proving repeated identical commands do not reuse requestId / do not drop the audit entry.

Controller raw review rejects E-2 Agent rework-2 despite commit a4cf3f8 fixing the audit requestId collision. Fresh evidence: targeted tests and build pass, and the new test proves repeated identical commands no longer reuse commandHash-derived requestId. However E-2 also requires sandbox degradation to be explicit end-to-end. Source review shows src/tools/runtime/handlers/terminal.ts still overwrites any sandboxExecutor-provided diagnostics with { sandboxed: true, fallbackUsed: false } at the executor path, so the later Alembic ToolContextFactory bridge cannot surface sandboxed=false/degradeReason even if it is repaired. Current tests only cover missing sandboxExecutor fallback, not executor-returned degradation. This is a new root-cause finding after two reworks, not a plain bounce: the producer contract must preserve optional executor diagnostics and add a regression before the Alembic consumer package can be valid.
